text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash rules out a solution to the Cyprus problem in the next few months - according to interview he gave to the Turkish Daily News newspaper.
- Police are to charge a Turk with espionage. Another two held in connection with the same case were released.
- Communist Akel is to reject a government proposal that high ranking state officials get a 29 percent pay rise.

- The Turkish side has not budged from its positions on the Cyprus issue, while foreign mediators attribute their stand on the inertness of the United States. The UN pushes for the adoption of goodwill measures by the two sides for the US to buy time.
- Swiss company Swatch offers one million francs for the 1600 rare Swatch pieces that disappeared en route to Cyprus.
- Pay rises to senior state officials will set a bad precedent, if approved by parliament. It will spark a chain reaction with pay demands from all levels of the civil service.
- Britain proposes a freeze on spending of the national guard with a paralell decline in the number of Turkish troops in Cyprus as a first step towards demilitarisation.
